title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
why_read: An ambitious framework turning research papers into executable, gradeable environments to benchmark and train AI systems that do science.
analysis: The authors convert 1,000 research papers into runnable environments where an AI agent's proposed method is graded against the original human-authored result, creating a scalable benchmark for 'AI scientists'. They report current frontier AI systems already beat the original human results 74% of the time on these reproduced tasks, which is a strong and somewhat surprising claim worth scrutinizing. They also use the resulting trace data to improve a smaller model's research ideation ability substantially. The idea of making the scientific literature 'runnable' rather than just readable is an interesting direction for AI-for-science research, though the 74% figure needs careful interpretation given how the baselines were constructed.
